title: Eliminate per-bitline latches: shared time-to-digital bitline sensing
idea: Remove the cross-coupled latch from every bitline pair. After charge sharing, each bitline gates a single discharge transistor onto a shared ramp, and one time-to-digital converter, time-interleaved over 32 bitlines in about 4 ns, records which bitlines cross threshold first. A global restore bus then rewrites the cells through one-transistor restore switches.
why: Periphery (fact 7): SA stripes are ~10-15% of the die; replacing 6-8 matched transistors per pair with 2 small devices cuts SA area ~50-60% (die -5-8%). Costs +2-4 ns latency.

title: Eliminate dummy mats: auto-zeroed self-referenced open-bitline sensing
idea: Remove the reference bitline and the half-populated dummy arrays that 6F2 open-bitline mats need at their edges. Each SA samples its own bitline onto a 2 fF capacitor just before the wordline rises and again after charge sharing, and a switched-capacitor comparator decides on the difference, cancelling SA offset and precharge error in the same step.
why: Edge dummy mats cost ~3-5% of die area; offset cancellation recovers ~30 mV of margin, so Cs can drop ~20% (fact 1) or bitlines can grow longer.

title: Eliminate row decoders: token-passing wordlines for streaming memory tiers
idea: For sequential tiers (AI weights, KV-cache streams, checkpoints), remove the row decoder tree. Each wordline driver holds a one-bit token in a 2-transistor dynamic stage and passes it to the next row on every activate clock, so rows open in a fixed order. A 'jump' tap every 512 rows allows coarse seeks.
why: Removes the row decoder and predecoder (~4-6% of die) and ~15 address wires per mat. Random access is lost but streaming traffic (~80% of weight reads) keeps full bandwidth.

title: Eliminate the VPP charge pump with a shared bootstrap boost plate
idea: Run a common boost plate under all wordlines of a sub-array. The decoder drives the selected wordline to VDD (1.1 V) and floats it, while all unselected wordlines stay actively clamped low. A 1.1 V step on the boost plate then couples only the floating wordline up to ~2.8 V for the restore window, as in a bootstrapped driver.
why: Removes the VPP pumps (~3-5% of die, 30-40% efficient) and roughly halves wordline energy, because the boost charge comes from a single 1.1 V swing (facts 7 and 10).

title: Eliminate periphery from the DRAM fab: array-only wafers bonded per 32 bitlines
idea: Build the DRAM wafer with only cells, vertical access transistors and a 32:1 bitline mux made from the same vertical-channel devices. Each mux output lands on a 0.5-0.8 um hybrid-bond pad to a mature-node CMOS wafer that holds every sense amp, decoder, pump and I/O circuit.
why: Fact 7: the ~49% periphery area leaves the expensive DRAM wafer, and the DRAM flow drops its HKMG periphery and ~6-8 masks. Periphery can be built in U.S. 28-40 nm fabs; cost per bit -25-35%.

title: Eliminate the DLL and clock tree with delay-insensitive handshake I/O
idea: Replace the DRAM's DLL, clock distribution and read-preamble training with a 4-phase bundled-data handshake per byte lane. The die returns data with a completion strobe generated by a replica bitline that tracks the real array, so it needs no clock at all.
why: Removes the DLL and clock tree (~2-3% of area, 10-15% of always-on I/O power). Power-down exit becomes instant, and latency follows real silicon instead of worst-case guardbands (typical tRCD -10-20%).

title: Eliminate VDD/2 precharge: plate-pulsed sensing from grounded bitlines
idea: Hold bitlines at ground and delete the equalizer transistors and the VBLP generator. To read, pulse the segmented cell plate of the selected 512-cell sub-array upward (FeRAM-style plate-line drive). A '1' cell pushes more charge onto the floating bitline than a '0', against a half-plate-pulse dummy reference, and a ground-referenced NMOS stage resolves it.
why: Removes precharge/equalize current (~15-20% of activate energy) and the VBLP regulator (~1-2% area); a ground-precharged bitline also eases low-voltage operation (fact 10).

title: Eliminate per-column sense amps: charge-coupled shift readout to edge amplifier
idea: Under each row of storage nodes, run a buried-channel CCD register. On read, all cell charges of the row dump into the CCD and are clocked sideways (4-phase, ~1 GHz) to one floating-diffusion amplifier per 1,024 columns, which digitizes them in series. Restore uses reverse clocking.
why: Removes the SA stripes (-10-15% of die) for a bulk sequential tier. At 0.99999 transfer efficiency per stage, ~1% of the charge is lost over 1,024 stages, and a full row takes ~1 us, which suits weights and checkpoints but not random access.

title: Eliminate the latch: impact-ionization gain diode on each bitline
idea: Replace the cross-coupled latch with one p-i-n diode per bitline biased just below breakdown, in a gated Geiger mode. The ~30-100 mV charge-share signal shifts its avalanche delay, so a '1' fires a rail-to-rail pulse within ~0.5 ns while a '0' does not, and a quench transistor resets it.
why: Replaces a 6-transistor SA with 1 diode and 1 quench device (SA area -70%), and the sense charge is only a few fC. Dark counts, jitter and temperature drift are the risks.

title: Eliminate CMOS sense latches: resonant-tunneling-diode Goto pairs
idea: Two series resonant tunneling diodes (SiGe/Si or InGaAs, grown on the bonded periphery die) form a MOBILE/Goto-pair bistable whose midpoint ties to the bitline. When the shared clocked bias rises, the pair snaps in ~10 ps to the state set by the bitline imbalance, and the same NDR logic can do column muxing.
why: Replaces 4-6 MOSFETs with 2 RTDs (SA area -50%, sensing ~10x faster), attacking the periphery share (fact 7). Integrating RTDs and keeping their peak current uniform is hard.

title: Eliminate sub-wordline drivers: resonant LC wordlines with energy recovery
idea: Delete the sub-wordline driver stripes by making master wordlines low-resistance Ru lines that a single pass switch per row connects to a bank-wide resonant LC rail. The switch closes at the sinusoid trough and opens at its peak, so the wordline charges adiabatically and most of its energy returns to the tank on discharge.
why: SWD stripes are ~8-10% of the die. Adiabatic charging recovers ~60-70% of wordline CV2 energy, which is stuck by the 3 V wordline (fact 10).

title: Eliminate TSVs: infrared light links shining straight through thinned dies
idea: Silicon is transparent at 1.3 um, so bond InP micro-LEDs and place Ge photodiodes at the same x-y sites on every 30 um-thinned die, and each lane's beam passes vertically through a 12-high stack. Time slots or wavelengths pick which die speaks, so there are no TSV keep-out zones and no TSV yield loss.
why: Fact 6: attacks the TSV area tax and the 20-30% HBM yield loss and removes TSV etch and fill; target ~1 pJ/bit vertical links.

title: Eliminate temperature sensors and refresh timers: canary-row retention sentinels
idea: Delete the on-die thermal sensors, refresh-rate tables and fixed 64 ms timer. Each bank instead holds 4 canary rows built with ~60% of normal Cs, checked periodically, and the bank refreshes only when a canary loses its pattern. Refresh then tracks actual leakage, including the 13 fA tail, at the current temperature and voltage.
why: Fact 3: refresh is 16-33% of idle power. Under typical conditions the refresh rate falls 4-8x while worst-case cells stay guarded, and the thermal-sensor and ADC area goes away.

title: Eliminate row-hammer counter SRAM: leaky-capacitor analog activation integrators
idea: Replace the digital per-row activation counters (TRR/PRAC tables) with one analog integrator per 8-row group. Each ACT dumps a fixed charge packet, tapped from the wordline driver's own swing, onto a deliberately leaky MOS capacitor with a ~64 ms decay. When its voltage crosses a threshold inverter, the group's neighbors are refreshed.
why: Fact 9: protects at ~1k activations without counter SRAM/CAM (PRAC-style schemes cost several % of area plus timing). The integrator is 3 transistors per 8 rows, and its built-in decay matches the refresh window, so no reset logic is needed.

title: Eliminate the on-die command decoder: host drives raw array timing
idea: Remove the DRAM's command state machine, mode registers and timing counters. The die exposes raw controls (wordline enable, SA enable, precharge, column strobe) on a hybrid-bonded wide port. The host controller issues every edge with row-specific timing from a per-row strength map built by boot-time profiling.
why: Removes ~2-3% of area in command logic and cuts per-row tRCD/tRAS ~20-35%, since most rows are far from worst case. A new array generation also needs no new on-die logic.

title: Eliminate full-row activation with dual-gate cells selected by row AND column
idea: Give each access transistor a second gate tied to a column-segment select line, so a channel conducts only when both its wordline and its 64-bit column segment are high. Only the addressed bits share charge, sense and restore, instead of all 8,192 cells on the row.
why: Fact 8: cuts the 128x overfetch and ~5.9 pJ per useful bit to ~0.3-0.6 pJ, and SA activity drops ~95% on random reads; cell area grows ~30-50%.

title: Eliminate the restore phase: consume-on-read memory for single-use data
idea: Add a destructive-read command and 'read-once' regions whose sense amps never write back. Activations, gradient buffers, evicted KV entries and packets are read once, then the row is marked free, so the SA fires at low swing and the row closes right after the burst.
why: Restore is ~40-50% of row-cycle energy and tRAS (fact 8). For read-once traffic (~30-50% of accelerator traffic), row energy falls ~40% and bank occupancy ~35%, so fewer bits are needed per unit of throughput.

title: Eliminate redundancy fuses: spare-free dies with controller-side row retirement
idea: Strip spare rows and columns, eFuse/antifuse banks and repair CAMs from the die. Each die ships a bad-row bitmap measured at wafer test and stored in SPD flash, and the controller remaps failing rows into a reserved 0.5% of normal rows through a 4-way hashed remap table.
why: Removes repair logic and spare arrays (~3-5% of die) plus fuse-programming test time, and takes repair comparators off the decode path (-0.5 ns). Yield holds because remapping is flexible die-wide.

title: Eliminate probe pads and probe cards: optically powered contactless wafer test
idea: Give each die a 100 um coil and a small photovoltaic cell. Flood illumination powers whole wafers, and test patterns flow over near-field inductive links at ~1 Gb/s, so thousands of dies test in parallel untouched. Probe pads, their drivers and test-lane ESD disappear.
why: Test is ~8-12% of DRAM cost; massively parallel contactless test lifts tester throughput ~10x and frees ~1-2% of die area.

title: Eliminate the decoder tree: colliding-pulse time-of-flight row selection
idea: Launch pulses from both ends of a slow-wave RC delay line that runs past 512 wordline taps. The relative launch delay encodes the address and sets where the two pulses meet, and only at that tap does the summed amplitude exceed a threshold inverter that fires its wordline.
why: Replaces predecoders and decoders (~4-6% of die, ~13 address wires per mat) with 2 wires and one threshold device per row. Needs ~10 ps/row timing accuracy with PVT calibration.

title: Eliminate silicon periphery footprint: n-only oxide-TFT dynamic logic above array
idea: Drop PMOS entirely and build decoders, wordline drivers and column logic from n-type oxide-semiconductor TFTs in the BEOL directly over the cell array, using bootstrapped domino-style NMOS-only logic with capacitive self-boost loads. Sense amps stay in silicon.
why: Moves ~30-40% of the periphery off the silicon footprint, shrinking the die ~25-35% (fact 7). Oxide-TFT leakage near 1e-19 A/um lets dynamic nodes hold for milliseconds.

title: Eliminate refresh logic and wordline segmentation in a 77 K memory tier
idea: Run a liquid-nitrogen-cooled DRAM tier at 77 K, where access-transistor leakage collapses (retention of hours) and copper resistivity drops ~7x. That permits deleting the refresh controller, the sub-wordline driver stripes (4x longer wordlines) and half of the SA stripes (lower noise and mismatch).
why: Facts 3 and 7: removes refresh power and bandwidth loss, and the periphery area falls ~10-15%; LN2 cooling energy is partly offset by lower I/O resistance.

title: Eliminate the sense amplifier via negative-capacitance bitlines
idea: Put a thin ferroelectric HZO layer in series between each bitline and its parasitic shield, biased so its negative capacitance cancels ~60% of bitline capacitance. The charge-share signal rises from ~100 mV to ~300 mV, enough for a plain skewed-inverter pair instead of a matched latch.
why: SA offset-matching area goes away (SA -40%), or Cs can drop 2-3x at the same margin, attacking the capacitor charge wall (fact 1). Negative-capacitance stability and hysteresis are unproven.

title: Eliminate the isolation trench: grow periphery isolation by area-selective ALD
idea: Skip the fluorocarbon STI etch and the HF liner and oxide strips. Non-fluorinated alkyl-aminosilane inhibitor SAMs mark the device islands, and repeated inhibitor-refresh cycles of area-selective ALD grow ~80 nm Al2O3 isolation ridges only between them. Selective Si epitaxy (dichlorosilane/HCl) then raises the active areas level.
why: Removes the whole STI module (trench etch, liner, fill, heavy CMP) and every fluorine step in isolation; periphery front-end cost ~-30%.

title: Eliminate tungsten contact plugs with tall raised-epitaxy source/drain posts
idea: Pattern contact holes in an amorphous-carbon template with O2 plasma, then grow in-situ-doped Si:P/SiGe:B selective epitaxy (DCS/HCl/PH3/B2H6) up through them to ~80 nm, so the source/drain posts themselves reach M1. Ash the template and cap each post with NiSi.
why: Removes WF6 CVD and fluorocarbon contact etch for millions of periphery contacts, and with them tungsten (China ~80%) from the periphery.

title: Eliminate scanners for periphery: imprint with hydrocarbon-release molds
idea: Pattern the 40-100 nm periphery layers by jet-and-flash nanoimprint using an acrylate resist with no fluorinated surfactant and a mold anti-stick layer of octadecylsilane instead of the usual fluorosilane. Transfer the pattern with Cl2/HBr/O2 etches only.
why: Removes optical scanners, PFAS photoacid generators and fluorinated topcoats from ~10-15 periphery layers; litho capex on those layers ~-70% (fact 4).

title: Eliminate transistor sense latches: carbon-released NEMS bistable beams
idea: Each bitline pair drives the two electrodes of a ~2 um buckled TiN nano-beam above it. The charge-share imbalance plus a common pull-in bias snaps the beam to one side, where its contact pulls that bitline to the rail. The cavity is cut by O2-ashing an amorphous-carbon sacrificial layer, which replaces HF-vapor or XeF2 release.
why: Gives a sense latch with zero leakage and no Vt mismatch, stacked in BEOL over the bitlines (SA area -30%) at ~fJ per sense. Mechanical speed (10-50 ns) restricts it to dense, slow tiers.

title: Eliminate the dual gate oxide with drain-extended cascode wordline drivers
idea: Build every 3 V wordline-driver device as a thin-oxide drain-extended or two-high cascode transistor, so one gate oxidation serves the whole die. This removes the thick-oxide mask and its HF strip; pre-gate cleans use SC1/SC2 plus an in-situ H2 bake instead of HF-last.
why: Removes one mask, the HF strip and a gate-stack variant from the periphery (fact 7), at a ~10% area cost in drivers.

title: Eliminate vias in decoder routing: capacitively coupled dynamic signal layers
idea: Decoder and predecoder signals are pulses, so let them cross metal levels through overlap capacitors with 5 nm ALD Al2O3 between the layers instead of vias, with a keeper on each node restoring DC level. Only power rails use vias, placed in a few relaxed landing zones etched with BCl3/Cl2, and the wiring is subtractive Cl-etched Mo.
why: Removes most periphery via etches (normally fluorocarbon), barrier and fill steps; periphery BEOL cost ~-20% and via-yield failures disappear.

title: Eliminate half the sense-amp stripes with decomposable-polymer air-gap bitlines
idea: Pattern bitlines with Cl-based etch, fill between them with polynorbornene (a fluorine-free sacrificial polymer, patterned in O2), cap with TEOS oxide, and decompose the polymer at ~400 C. The air gaps cut bitline capacitance ~35%, so bitlines can be ~1.6x longer per SA and roughly every other SA stripe is deleted.
why: Removes ~5-6% of die area in SA stripes, or alternatively gives +50% signal to ease the Cs wall (fact 1).

title: Eliminate the switched-capacitor charge pump: on-die piezoelectric AlN transformer
idea: Replace each bank's VPP pump with a solidly mounted Rosen-type AlN piezoelectric transformer (~200 um, ~25 MHz resonance) that steps 1.1 V up to ~3 V at ~80% efficiency into a diode rectifier. AlN is sputtered and etched with Cl2/BCl3, and its Mo electrodes with Cl2/O2, with no release etch.
why: Pumps take ~3-5% of area at 30-40% efficiency, so VPP energy roughly halves and the large MOS pump capacitors go away (facts 7 and 10).

title: Eliminate multi-patterning in sense-amp stripes via block-copolymer self-assembly
idea: SA and column-select transistor arrays are periodic at bitline pitch, so define their gate and active lines by directed self-assembly of PS-b-PMMA guided by coarse KrF chemical prepatterns. Remove the PMMA with UV plus an acetic acid rinse and transfer with HBr/Cl2/O2, eliminating fluorocarbon SADP spacer etches and PAG resists.
why: Pitch-matched SAs below 30 nm without EUV or SADP (fact 4); SA-stripe patterning cost ~-40-60%.

title: Eliminate metal etch: pillar-first, catalyst-seeded electroless periphery wiring
idea: Photo-pattern an aminosilane SAM with UV-ozone and bind a Pd-ion catalyst only where lines and vias belong. Grow Co (with a Co-B cap) by electroless plating, build vias as plated pillars before the dielectric, spin-coat polysilazane-derived oxide over them, and polish to the pillar tops, so neither lines nor vias are ever etched.
why: Removes metal etch, via etch, fluorocarbon chemistry and Ta/W barriers from periphery BEOL; additive and few-tool, which suits the 60-200 nm periphery pitch.

title: Eliminate silicon oxide and nitride etching: chlorine-etchable periphery dielectrics
idea: In the periphery, swap the SiO2 and SiN that practically require fluorocarbon or HF to etch for dielectrics that etch in Cl/Br plasma or mild wet chemistry: Al2O3 and HfO2 (BCl3/Cl2), AlN (Cl2 or hot KOH) and amorphous-carbon hard masks (O2). SiO2 stays only where it is never etched (gap fill, lift-off).
why: Gives a fully fluorine-free periphery palette; Al2O3 and AlN also conduct heat ~10-100x better than SiO2. Their higher k is offset by air gaps.

title: Eliminate silicon wafers for periphery: LTPS-on-glass panels from display fabs
idea: Build DRAM periphery as laser-crystallized LTPS CMOS on Gen-6 glass in underused LCD/OLED fabs converted to wet etches (H3PO4/HNO3/acetic, oxalic) and Cl-only dry etch, with fluorine chamber cleans replaced by Cl2/O2. Dice the panels into tiles and bond them face-to-face over array dies at 2-5 um pitch through mux-concentrated bitline groups.
why: Display-fab area costs ~1/10 of silicon fab area, and LTPS mobility (~100 cm2/Vs) handles 200-400 MHz periphery, so periphery capital and cost per die fall sharply.

title: Eliminate decoder transistors: Schottky diode-matrix row decoding
idea: Build row predecode and decode as a classic diode-AND matrix of NiSi/n-Si Schottky diodes formed by self-aligned silicidation (unreacted Ni stripped in H2SO4/H2O2). Each decode node is dynamically precharged and pulled down by diodes on the complement address lines, so only the final wordline driver remains a transistor.
why: Cuts decoder transistor count ~70% and removes ~2 masks of gate and contact work in the decode zone, all etch-free (fact 7).

title: Eliminate high-k metal-gate periphery: slow, wide internal buses with poly/SiON
idea: Make the internal datapath 8x wider at 1/8 the clock (a 4,096-bit, 400 MHz bonded port), so periphery transistors can be plain poly-Si/SiON at 65-90 nm-class speed. Gates are etched with HBr/Cl2 and spacers are Al2O3 etched with BCl3, removing gate-last HKMG, dual work-function metals and their fluorinated steps.
why: Periphery masks -4-6 and steps ~-20%, buildable on legacy U.S. tools; wide-slow I/O also cuts interface energy ~3x (fact 5).

title: Eliminate metal etching: anodization-defined aluminum periphery wiring
idea: Deposit blanket Al, mask the line regions with PAG-free DNQ/novolak i-line resist, and anodize the exposed metal fully into Al2O3 in citric or boric acid. The converted oxide becomes the insulator between lines, giving a planar wiring level with no metal etch, no gap fill and no CMP.
why: Removes etch, fill and CMP from 2-3 periphery signal levels using abundant Al (no W, Cu or Ta), and the planar levels ease stacking.

title: Eliminate deep-trench decoupling capacitors with traveling-wave sense-amp firing
idea: Fire the 8k SAs of a row as a wave crossing the mat over ~2 ns, each SA enabling its neighbor through a delay cell, so the 1-2 A sensing spike becomes a flat ramp. Supply droop falls ~5x, so deep-trench decaps (which need SF6 Bosch etch) and most MOS decaps are deleted; the remaining flow uses Cl-based etches.
why: Removes ~2-4% of die in decaps, and the lower droop lets the array voltage margin shrink (fact 10); the first-needed column is fired first to hide latency.

title: Eliminate column decoders and CSL wiring: sense latches as shift registers
idea: After sensing, chain the SA latches into a two-phase shift register (2 transfer gates per SA), so the row buffer clocks out serially to 64 edge taps. The column decoder, the column-select lines and one metal/via level disappear, and the remaining wiring is Cl-etched Al/Mo.
why: Removes the column decoder and CSL (~3-5% of die) and one BEOL level; whole-row streaming suits AI weights, while random-word latency rises.

title: Eliminate fluorinated test fluids: self-heating hammer-pattern thermal screening
idea: Hot test and burn-in normally rely on PFPE (Galden/Fluorinert) chillers and baths. Instead each die heats itself to 95-125 C with an all-bank activate pattern (~1-2 W), closed-loop on an on-die ring-oscillator thermometer, so handlers need only air-cooled chucks and retention screens run at true temperature.
why: Removes PFAS heat-transfer fluids from test floors and cuts handler capex ~30%; the pattern also screens hammer-weak rows (fact 9).

title: Eliminate copper and tungsten: oxygen-patterned multilayer graphene periphery lines
idea: Grow 10-20-layer graphene on a Co catalyst at BEOL temperature, intercalation-dope it with FeCl3, and pattern it with O2 plasma, since carbon needs no halogen etch. The lines need no Ta/TaN barrier and resist electromigration.
why: Removes W (China ~80%), Cu and Ta from local periphery wiring with the simplest fluorine-free etch; at sub-30 nm widths doped graphene avoids copper's size-effect resistivity rise.

title: Eliminate address buses: two-wire analog voltage row addressing
idea: Replace the ~13 predecoded address lines per mat with two analog wires (16 coarse and 32 fine levels) and a resistive ladder. Each wordline driver ANDs two 2-transistor window comparators tied to its ladder taps and fires only when both broadcast voltages fall in its window; the wiring is Cl-etched Mo.
why: Removes the predecoders (decoder area -40%) and the metal level that hosts the address bus; noise margin needs ladder calibration.

title: Eliminate plasma fin etch: crystallographic TMAH wet-etched sense-amp transistors
idea: On the bonded periphery wafer, use (110) silicon, where TMAH etches vertical {111} sidewalls at ~100:1 anisotropy, to form SA fins through an Al2O3 hard mask patterned with BCl3. The fins come out with atomically smooth walls and no fluorinated or HBr plasma.
why: Smooth walls cut Vt mismatch ~20-30%, so SA devices can shrink at the same offset; the fin plasma-etch module disappears.

title: Eliminate the voltage-mode latch: selective-epitaxy bipolar pre-amp in bitline contact
idea: Form a vertical n-p-n inside each bitline contact by in-situ-doped selective epitaxy (DCS/HCl with PH3/B2H6, avoiding BF2 implants), with the bitline driving the base. The charge-share signal becomes a collector current (beta ~50) into one shared current comparator per 16 bitlines, and a shared write driver restores the cells.
why: Cuts SA latch count 16x (die -8-10%) with ~2 ns sensing, and drops fluorinated BF2 implant species from the periphery.

title: Eliminate PFAS permitting drag: fluorine-free periphery fast-lane policy
idea: Create a federal/state permitting fast lane and cost share for DRAM periphery lines certified fluorine-free (Cl/Br/O etches, MoO2Cl2 metal, PAG-free resists, Cl2/O2 chamber cleans, PFPE-free test). Publish it as an open reference flow with shared yield data, so new U.S. periphery fabs avoid PFAS-driven permit delays and EU restriction risk.
why: Permitting is ~1-2 years of a 3-5-year fab timeline. Paired with array-only fabs, this puts ~49% of DRAM die area into plants that are faster to build in the U.S.
